title: Verify a tool/guard: howto (T2)
desc: Howto tier of verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static: the step-by-step verify-before-merge sequence for the three modes (synthetic/live/static).
steps: STOP -- READ THIS BEFORE YOU EDIT THIS SKILL. It scores 61 of 100 (2026-08-29 measurement; age-decayed to 56 by 2026-09-27 -- refreshed 2026-09-27 wkappbot-kih) against a HARD FLOOR OF 60, and 128 study locks in WkAutoQuant's CLAUDE.md name it. One point lower and ALL 128 BREAK AT ONCE, making every file they protect unedittable repo-wide. Measured 2026-08-29: git show origin/main:CLAUDE.md piped to grep -c on this skill id returns 128, and the study-lock board printed by reading any locked source shows the live score. BUT DO NOT PANIC, AND HERE IS THE MEASUREMENT THAT CORRECTS AN EARLIER OVER-ALARM OF MINE: the score does NOT decay on its own, it moves only when someone edits, and BOTH ordinary edit paths are already safe. --add-step is refused below 70 by skilledit-guard. --find/--replace is exempt, but I tested it four ways on 2026-08-29 -- adding cross-links, adding runnable commands, cutting ~500 bytes, and cutting a whole passage -- and the score did not move by a single point in any direction. THE SCORE IS STEP-COUNT DRIVEN, NOT BYTE DRIVEN: 32 steps against a 20-step ceiling is what holds it at 61, so shaving prose is wasted effort. AND A THIRD VERIFICATION SHAPE, measured 2026-09-03 and cheap enough to be a habit: RE-RUN THE FAILING COMMAND BEFORE BRIEFING A FIX FOR IT. A FOURTH SHAPE, measured 2026-09-03 and the cheapest of all: A PROBE THAT CANNOT FAIL PROVES NOTHING, SO TAKE THE BASELINE FIRST. Folding eleven identical harness:skill blocks into one brace-glob, I verified coverage survived by attempting an Edit on a folded member and reading the absence of a refusal as success. It was not: an UNTOUCHED single-file rule produced the identical non-refusal, because the Edit tool bypasses harness:skill by a hole this catalog already documents at harness-edit-write-skill-bypass. The check could not have failed either way. What actually settled it was calling the resolver directly -- dot-source wkharness-common-skilllock.ps1 and run Get-WkClaudeMdMatchedSkills against each member -- and for an inline migration, reading the migrated source's own head for its three wkappbot skill read lines. THE RULE: before trusting a negative result, run the SAME probe against a case you know should come out positive. A FIFTH SHAPE, measured 2026-09-03 landing a filter into a 400-plus-line host: VERIFY A SIZE CONSTRAINT WITH wc -l, NEVER BY READING THE DIFF. fat-source-growth refuses ANY net growth of a fat file, even one line, so an extraction must land the host at its committed length EXACTLY. The diff looked correct at every intermediate step and the host was still 442 lines against a committed 358; only the count said so. The technique that hit zero was to make the seam REPLACE an existing blank line rather than be inserted beside it -- one line out, one line in. And the honest failure mode to plan for: an extraction is a TRANSACTION, not a step, because midway through it the host can hold a member the new module also defines, which is a CS0111 break rather than a partial improvement. Stage every fragment file first, run the edits back to back, and if you are forced to stop midway, restore the host with git checkout HEAD rather than leaving a canonical source that does not compile; if both agree, you have measured your instrument rather than your subject. Two sectors dispatched at descent came back reporting that the defects they were sent to repair no longer existed -- wk-cost fills returned 70 executions for a past date the record called broken, and recovery_debt_seed printed 25 of 25 where the record said 23 with two named failures, both with no working-tree change. An inherited OPEN item is a CLAIM WITH A DATE ON IT, never a fact, and half a dispatch budget went to establishing that. The same session also wrote each result INTO the tool that produced it rather than only into a letter, because a verification nobody wrote down is one the next session pays for again. THE ONLY LEVER THAT WORKS is reducing the NUMBER of steps: archive a step's content into verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static-ref FIRST, then --delete-step it here with the verbatim quote the guard demands -- a copy-then-delete is a MOVE, not the knowledge loss this repo forbids. Start with step 17, which at 15,092 bytes is a concatenation of several merged incidents and is the clearest single candidate. Until someone does that, this skill is STABLE at 61 and the 128 locks hold. DECISION: every guard's self-test must include PROSE-IMMUNITY fixtures built from the guard's own commit message and block text. WHEN: you are writing the test suite for any guard that matches command strings. HOW: after the block and allow fixtures, add cases that feed the guard sentences DESCRIBING what it forbids -- a git commit whose message quotes the rule, a wkappbot suggest reporting the bug, an echo containing the remedy arrow this skill's own messages print -- and assert ALLOW, then add the same shapes as REAL chained commands and assert BLOCK, so the anchor is proven to cut one way only; run wkappbot skill read claude-md-harness-rules for the command-start anchoring discipline these fixtures enforce. WHY: measured 2026-08-01 on the emergency9 guard. It refused the commit message documenting itself within an hour of being written, because the message contained the words it forbids, and two more anchor defects surfaced from the same class -- the git checks anchored the word git but let a wildcard reach into a quoted message, and the remedy arrow was read as a shell redirect onto CLAUDE.md. The deletion block in wkharness-claude-main.ps1 already recorded this exact failure against its own first version, so the trap was documented and still cost a turn to rediscover from the other side. A rule that cannot be written about is a rule that stops being maintained, and the cheapest permanent proof against it is a fixture cut from the guard's own prose.

DECISION: when a tool's output is a MODEL'S ANSWER, stop trying to assert the output and verify the deterministic SHELL around it, then treat the answer as data about the INPUT. WHEN: building or reviewing any wk tool that calls a real model, such as bin/wkwhatdidyouinherit.ps1 added 2026-08-21, which asks a fresh cheap session the owner's handoff question at session start. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for the three modes and wkappbot skill read wkareyouready for the sibling that deliberately spawns nothing, then live-fire the SHELL -- run once expecting the skip path and once expecting the ask path and SEE both with your own eyes, confirm a missing input exits non-zero rather than cheerfully zero, and confirm output STREAMS rather than buffering. WHY: measured while building that tool, where two defects hid in exactly the places the three usual modes do not look. Its start gate silently never fired across three fixes because a regex character class lost its backslash to shell escaping, and every run still LOOKED successful since the tool simply proceeded to ask -- a gate that never fires is indistinguishable from a gate that passes unless you have watched it refuse. Separately two runs sat silent past 120 seconds because the CLI output went through Out-String, which buffers the whole answer, so the watcher saw a frozen prompt; streaming was the fix and is itself a verifiable property. THE GENERAL RULE worth carrying: with a non-deterministic core, the output is not the thing under test -- here, how far an UNINSTRUCTED model travelled measures the letter and the skill tree it read, not the model.

A MEASUREMENT IS ONLY AS GOOD AS THE CONTEXT IT RAN IN, and the failure runs in BOTH directions -- measured 2026-09-04. TWO MORE DIRECTIONS OF IT, 2026-09-14, and both cost me a wrong answer in front of the owner. FIRST, A COMPONENT NUMBER IS NOT A SHARE OF THE WHOLE: I had profiled an identity lookup at 3189 ms and told him that was why a letter commit took seventeen minutes. The hook's own stopwatch put the ladder at 216830 ms, so that lookup was ONE AND A HALF PERCENT and fixing it alone would have moved seventeen minutes to sixteen minutes fifty-eight seconds. The real weight sat in two gates, 117142 ms and 90127 ms, ninety-six percent between them -- and I had ranked them in the wrong ORDER too, from reading the source instead of timing it. SECOND, AND SUBTLER: after fixing the larger gate I re-ran and read 195244 against 216830, a ten percent cut, while the gate itself went 117142 to 73423. THOSE TOTALS ARE NOT COMPARABLE -- the letter had GROWN between runs because I was restoring paragraphs into it, and both gates cost O(paragraphs times tokens), so the OTHER gate rose from 90127 to 114246 on its own. A before-and-after is a measurement only while the SUBJECT is unchanged; when it moved, report the per-component figure and say the totals are not the same measurement rather than quoting whichever number flatters you. THE FINDING THAT FELL OUT OF IT is worth more than either number: editing the letter was itself making the next commit slower. Verifying a memoised committer-model lookup by actually running it, exactly as this skill demands, I got value = [] with five calls at 13.85, 16.59, 10.81, 11.09 and 11.37 ms, and reported the safety control FAILED. It had not failed: a bare PowerShell subprocess carries no harness lineage, so a blank return was CORRECT, and five calls holding steady near 11 ms instead of collapsing to 0.2 ms was the memo REFUSING to cache a blank -- precisely the safety property under test. This skill's documented trap is trusting a green proto the live path would fail; this is its MIRROR IMAGE, condemning a healthy module because the harness that feeds it was absent. Both come from the same unasked question: what does this function READ, and is that input present in the process I am running it in? Ask it before believing any blank or any zero, and if the input is missing, report the number AND the missing input in one sentence, never the number alone. The one finding that survived was context-free and therefore sound -- the canonical host contained ZERO occurrences of the cached function's name, and a string is absent or present no matter who runs the grep. AND THE SHARPEST FORM OF IT, measured the same day: A REFUSE-CASE ASSERTION MUST DISTINGUISH AN ABSENT FUNCTION FROM A REFUSAL, or it passes against an empty file. Promoting a guard from its proto name to canonical broke the selftest's dot-source, which still named the PROTO file. Run from the canonical path the subject was never defined, and the suite printed The term Resolve-WkPromotionPath is not recognized followed by PASS empty path, PASS null path, PASS quote in path, PASS asterisk in path, PASS angle brackets in path, PASS pipe in path, RESULT 6 of 9. SIX REFUSE CASES PASSED WITH NO CODE AT ALL -- a missing function returns nothing, and the suite read nothing as correctly refused. The 9 of 9 measured minutes earlier at the PROTO path was three real passes plus six that proved only the absence of a function, and it is not detectable there because at the proto path both readings coincide. TWO RULES FALL OUT. First, a suite must ASSERT ITS SUBJECT EXISTS -- Get-Command after the dot-source, and abort non-zero with zero PASS lines if it does not, because a suite whose subject is missing must ABORT rather than score. Second, this is exactly why a promoted thing is run from the CANONICAL path and never from the proto's: promotion is the event that makes absent and refused differ, so the proto run is structurally blind to it. AND WHEN YOU BREAK SOMETHING ON PURPOSE, BREAK THE SUBJECT, NEVER THE RECOVERY -- measured 2026-09-04. Proving a post-hook guard that detects a failed module load, I isolated the hook into an empty directory so its siblings would be missing. Nothing printed, and silence read as the guard not working. The guard was fine: its own recovery module lives beside it, so the empty directory removed THAT too, its presence check returned false, and the entire block was skipped by design. The fix was to place the recovery module beside the isolated copy and remove only the module UNDER TEST, after which it printed both lines and the dirty file was genuinely restored, confirmed by a clean git status and a marker count of zero rather than by the guard's own output. THE RULE: a negative test must remove exactly the thing the guard WATCHES and keep everything the guard NEEDS, or you have tested the scaffolding; and read the tree, not the message, because output is a claim and the working copy is the fact. SAME ROOT, DIFFERENT SURFACE: A TIMING GATE MUST TIME THE HOT PATH, NOT THE BRANCH YOU EDITED -- measured 2026-08-29, and the gate PASSED while proving nothing. A diagnostic was moved below the early returns so it could not run on ordinary calls, and the gate timed it ABOVE the threshold with the suppress switch on: 0.02ms, PASS. True and irrelevant -- above the threshold is the BLOCK path, reached only when already refusing, while the path taken on EVERY call returns null below it. Timing the branch you changed feels like diligence and is the same error as asserting on a function you never called. Name the most frequently executed path, time THAT against the unmodified original, and print both -- one number cannot show a regression. SECOND TRAP in the same run: a proto executed from .tmp resolves dependencies relative to .tmp, so the delegation predicate never loaded, the exemption silently vanished, and the candidate measured 198ms against the original's 19ms. The comparison was invalid AND its invalidity was indistinguishable from a real 10x regression. Pass the dependency root explicitly or run from CANONICAL: a proto that cannot find its dependency does not error, it quietly takes another branch. INCIDENT 2026-08-29, A SECOND INSTANCE THE SAME DAY, and it is the sharpest form of this rule: an EQUIVALENCE test between an old path and a new path passes perfectly when the NEW PATH IS DEAD, because a fallback makes both run the same code. Wiring an indexer into a harness guard produced a self-test reporting 4 of 4 with a genuine inversion control that varied the skill id and watched counts move from 5 to 0 -- and it was still worthless. The seam probed for the indexer under a home-directory path that does not exist, so its Test-Path was always false and the entire cache block was skipped on every call. Two more defects hid behind that one, invisible for the same reason: the freshness check compared the cache's INDEXING TIME against the file's mtime as an equality test, which could not match even to the second, and the update call never stored an mtime at all, so the compared value was never written. Three bugs, one fatal, and a green suite over all of them. THE RULE: agreement between two paths proves they AGREE, never that both RAN. Any test whose subject is an alternative path must first prove the alternative was TAKEN -- make it emit a marker, count its invocations, or point it at a POISONED cache holding a deliberately wrong value, since a live cache path then returns the wrong number while a dead one silently returns the right one from the fallback. THE ORIGINAL ENTRY FOLLOWS. THE PROBE IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE CLAIM: four probe-not-subject fail: four probe-not-subject failures in one session, twice printing FAIL over working code and once PASS over the wrong path. (1) An allow-path assertion looked for launcher text in a value the gate returns as null BY DESIGN. (2) A marker was checked outside the function that dot-sourced it, and a dot-source inside a function scopes to that function. (3) A Stop-hook number came from a synthetic test launcher, two orders of magnitude below the live path, exactly as that skill's own step already warned. (4) A helper named R bound silently to PowerShell's built-in alias for Invoke-History, so every case invoked the wrong command. WHEN: your suite contradicts a change you have good reason to believe is correct. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for the structural-validity-is-not-runtime-correctness rule, then read the FIRST error line rather than the tally -- the binding error named Invoke-History in plain text -- and ask what the subject returns on the exact path the probe exercises. Never single-letter a helper in PowerShell. THE RULE EARNED: a test makes two claims, one about the subject and one about ITSELF, and the second is the one to check first. ALSO INCIDENT: a measurement instrument MUTATED its own subject, and its answer measured the wrong thing -- both defects sat in the shell around the model, exactly where step 7 says to look. WHEN: you build or review a tool that asks a fresh model a question ABOUT an artifact in order to score that artifact. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for the three modes, then give the spawned model a READ-ONLY seat and, before reading any score into its reply, assert what the reply is a measurement OF -- and confirm authorship of any side effect by a second independent signal such as file mtime, never by the child's own report. WHY: measured live 2026-08-21 on bin/wkwhatdidyouinherit.ps1, which spawns a fresh claude -p to grade HANDOFF.md. The spawned Sonnet EDITED HANDOFF.md, adding an 18-line Article 14 correction to the very letter it was hired to assess; the content was good and the authorship held up under a second measurement (mtime 02:33:53 fell inside the child's live window, last write 02:38:03), so this is not a claim of damage but a claim that the instrument has a side effect on its subject and therefore cannot be re-run against the same artifact twice for the same reading. SECOND AND WORSE, the visible reply was not an answer at all but the CHILD SESSION'S OWN STOP-HOOK LABELS, and the child said so in its own words -- this turn is the Stop hook repeat-demand, not a new instruction -- so the tool was scoring HOOK COMPLIANCE while its author believed it was scoring letter readability, inverting step 7's premise that an uninstructed model's travel distance measures the letter. GENERAL SHAPE: when you point a model at a target and read its output as a measurement, the HARNESS around that model is also in the loop, and a harness that demands output will supply output that is not the measurement you wanted. Pairs with step 8 -- an absent timeout is invisible until a human runs out of patience. MERGED HERE 2026-08-24, same class -- an instrument that measures the wrong subject, this time in TIME rather than in state: A GHA-LOG VERDICT IS WORTHLESS UNLESS THE RUN'S START TIME IS COMPARED AGAINST THE PROMOTION TIME. WHEN widened by OR: this also fires when you are about to conclude from a relay log that a promoted seam is absent or dead, or when reading any report that says ABSENT about a tag. THE ADDED HOW: for every run you cite, put its createdAt beside the promotion timestamp and say which is earlier -- a cycle that CLONED BEFORE a commit cannot print that commit's tag, so its zero means NOT-YET-TESTABLE and never ABSENT; and NEVER grep a run whose status is in_progress, because gh serves no log at all until completion, so that empty result proves nothing. MEASURED 2026-08-24: a delegate examined relay runs 32653825201 at 17:07Z and 32652842147 at 16:48Z and reported pending-sell-stage as ABSENT SEAM NOT WIRED and loss-ratio-amend as ABSENT PATH NOT EXECUTING -- both runs started BEFORE the 17:31Z promotion of the very seam under test, and the report tabulated those start times without ever comparing them to anything. It also labelled a SUNDAY cycle US regular hours TRADEABLE purely because the UTC clock matched the session window. THE DANGEROUS PART IS WHAT IT GOT RIGHT: its third verdict, loss-ratio-mult at 1466, matched ROOT's independent count exactly, so a report verifiable in one place earns trust it has not earned in the others -- CHECK EACH VERDICT SEPARATELY. And reach first for the tag that CAN be tested with the market shut: a per-cycle write prints whether or not a market is open, while an amend needs live order flow, so their zeros mean entirely different things. //why:Registering two green suites in the official verifier made a SIXTH suite visible at 8 of 14, all six failures being REFUSE cases returning an empty verdict.-opus //why:the letter-edit slowness looked like a 25 s gate but a replayed hook showed 142 ms there with a fresh cache; the spike was the stale-cache refresh, fixed by deciding non-letter paths first-opus //why:age-reset for tier-gate clearance: score 56<60 due to 7-day decay on 33-step howto, cleanbaseline OwnPaths lineage wiring in progress-sonnet

DECISION: give a spawned model a WHITELIST seat, never a blacklist, and then watch it be REFUSED before believing the seat exists. WHEN: any tool that spawns a real model against your own repo, especially one left running unattended or backgrounded with a keystroke. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for the live-versus-static split, then pass claude's --tools with an explicit allow-list such as Read,Grep,Glob rather than --disallowedTools, and live-fire it once by asking the child to CREATE a file and asserting the file is absent afterwards -- the flag being present in the command line is not the same fact as the write being refused. WHY: measured 2026-08-21 on bin/wkwhatdidyouinherit.ps1, which spawns a fresh session to grade HANDOFF.md and whose child EDITED that letter mid-run. --disallowedTools is a deny-list, so every tool the author forgets stays reachable, and the tools the author forgets are exactly the ones the incident will use; --tools names what is allowed and everything else is closed by construction. THE COST, stated because it is real: this tool's whole measurement is how far an UNINSTRUCTED model travels unprompted, and its two best recorded runs used tools to get there -- one checked the disk unbidden, one spawned its own delegate -- so a tight whitelist buys safety by narrowing exactly the signal being measured. Read,Grep,Glob keeps the go-and-check behaviour and drops the spawn-a-delegate behaviour; Bash would restore reach but reopens writing, since a shell redirect is a write. //why:The post-edit verb was believed only after one call that had to pass (dry-run rc 0) and one that had to stay refused (remove 2520 rc 2) both ran from the canonical path.-sonnet //why:The post-edit verb was believed only after one call that had to pass (dry-run rc 0) and one that had to stay refused (remove 2520 rc 2) both ran from the canonical path.-sonnet

A VERIFICATION IS NOT FINISHED WHEN THE CHECK PASSES -- IT IS FINISHED WHEN YOU KNOW WHAT WOULD ERASE THE RECORD OF IT, and for any file with a DEPLOY MASTER the answer is usually the next deploy. Measured 2026-09-07 on bin/wkclaude.ps1: its comment carries a claim about THREE files and grep -c seenPrompt still returned 4 in the repo copy and in BOTH deploy masters, so the claim is true -- but a change DELETING that three-file note appeared in the working tree TWICE in one session, neither time made by the session, so something REGENERATES the removal. ANSWERED 2026-09-07, THIRD OCCURRENCE, AND IT COST ONE grep: NEITHER DEPLOY MASTER CARRIES THE NOTE. wkappbot-kih/tools/wrappers/wkclaude.ps1 and personal-docs/tools/wrappers/wkclaude.ps1 both exist, both predate the repo copy, and a recursive grep for the note text across BOTH tools trees returns ZERO files. So every deploy overwrites bin/wkclaude.ps1 with a copy that never had the note, and the deletion is not a session, a hook or a race -- it is the deploy doing exactly what it is built to do. IDENTICAL MECHANISM TO bin/wkask.sh, corrupted eleven times before anyone checked whether the corrupted copy WAS the install master. THE GENERAL RULE, and it is the cheap half of this step: for any repo file with a DEPLOY MASTER, an edit is not landed until the MASTER carries it -- grep the master for your own text before believing the change survived, because the repo copy is downstream and a deploy is a silent revert. THE CROSS-REPO BOUNDARY STILL HOLDS: the masters live in other repos, so this is a REPORT and never an edit. AND THE PROOF GOT STRONGER THE SAME HOUR, FOURTH OCCURRENCE: after parking the deletion in a stash, it reappeared within about five minutes, and this time the identification is exact rather than circumstantial. bin/wkclaude.ps1 came back at 8083 bytes with mtime 2026-09-06 01:17:10.760915300, BYTE-COUNT AND TIMESTAMP IDENTICAL to wkappbot-kih/tools/wrappers/wkclaude.ps1 -- so it is a timestamp-preserving copy FROM that master, not an edit, not a hook rewriting the region, and not a session. The personal-docs master is a different size, 8032, which rules it out as the source. THE TECHNIQUE WORTH REUSING, and it is cheaper than any content diff: when a file keeps reverting, ls the candidate sources with full-iso timestamps beside the victim and look for an EXACT match on BOTH size and mtime -- a copy that preserves mtime names its own source, while a content diff only tells you what changed. DO NOT KEEP RE-STASHING: the parking remedy treats a symptom that regenerates on a timer, so record the source and leave the repo copy alone, since it will be overwritten again regardless. Same mechanism as bin/wkask.sh, corrupted eleven times before anyone found that the corrupted copy WAS the install master. HANDLE THE STRAY CHANGE THIS WAY: git checkout -- is refused in this repo and rightly so, since an unexpected working-tree change is usually a sibling session's live edit; park it with git stash push -- <path> under a FINDABLE MESSAGE, never an index, and write into the file's own comment that the parked change must not be landed and why. INCIDENT: my OWN absence-check gave a false pass, on the very night I wrote the rule against absence-checks -- the file was missing because the command never ran. WHEN: you assert that something did NOT happen, especially that a file was not written, a process did not survive, or a marker did not appear. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static, then capture the EXIT CODE of the action under test and assert it FIRST -- an absence is only evidence once you have proved the thing you were testing actually executed; and for a CLI, make the command echo something on success so a zero-output run cannot be mistaken for a clean one. A throw there is swallowed by the outer catch and silently takes the rest of the block with it. WHEN: any suite whose cases differ only by a FIXTURE THE SUBJECT LOADS BY PATH -- a ledger, a config, a cache, a session file -- and above all when the cases agree with each other suspiciously well. THE TELL WAS IN ITS OWN PASTED OUTPUT: a case paying one of two skills MUST print 1 of 2, so 0 of 2 there proves the fixture was never read, and no agreement among the other cases survives that. THE RULE: TWO IDENTICAL RESULTS ARE EVIDENCE OF DETERMINISM ONLY AFTER THE INPUTS ARE PROVEN DIFFERENT, and a suite where every case fails to bind its fixture is maximally self-consistent and entirely uninformative. THE CONTROL IS WHAT CATCHES IT, which is why the control is never optional: that module returns null on every error path, so NOT RUNNING and DEBT PAID are indistinguishable, and an implementation refusing unconditionally passes every case except the control. WHEN: a delegate returns a green suite for a function taking a configuration argument -- a port, a path, a mode, a timeout -- and you are deciding whether to promote it. DECISION: before you believe a failing case, check that it CREATES the condition it names -- three cases in one suite did not, and each cost a round. WHEN: a case keeps failing across rounds while the code around it changes, or a tally rises while the failure SET moves. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for the mode definitions, then read the fixture and the case NAME together and ask whether a CORRECT implementation could possibly pass; check that every value the fixture declares is actually PASSED to the subject, and that the assertion's arguments bind the way the helper's signature expects. DECISION: a suite that checks only the SHAPE of an extracted value passes while the feature stays dead -- assert that the value can be FOUND in its real target. WHEN: you are testing any parser, extractor or matcher whose output is later used to LOCATE something -- an anchor, a key, a path, an id. HOW: run wkappbot skill read verify-tool-or-guard-synthetic-live-static for the mode definitions, then add one case that takes the extracted value and searches the ACTUAL artifact for it, asserting the hit count is at least one; a case comparing the extraction against a literal you also wrote proves the two literals match and nothing more. WHY: measured 2026-09-05 in wkappbot-kih on the like-why anchor extractor. Its pattern took one run of non-space characters, so for a quoted multi-word fragment it returned a double-quote plus a single letter and stopped. Every shape assertion would have passed. What exposed it was searching the target skill for the extracted anchor: ZERO steps contained it while exactly ONE contained the full fragment, and the feature had therefore written nothing for five weeks across the entire catalogue. THE GENERALISATION WORTH KEEPING: an extractor's contract is not that it returns a string, it is that it returns THE string that unlocks the next step, so the test must attempt that next step.
